title: 1998 AHSME Problem 12
statement: How many different prime numbers are factors of \(N\) if \[ \log_2(\log_3(\log_5(\log_7N)))=11? \]

solutions.text: Successively exponentiating gives \[ N=7^{\,5^{\,3^{\,2^{11}}}}. \] Thus \(7\) is the only prime factor of \(N,\) so the correct answer is A.
hints: Undo the logarithms one at a time, starting with base \(2\)
The final expression for \(N\) is a power of \(7\)
